narrative:
The decision regarding your law school application was influenced by a prediction indicating a 77.4% likelihood that you would fail the bar exam if you were to take it. This high probability of failure is a significant factor in the admissions process, as it suggests that you may struggle to meet the requirements necessary for success in the legal field.

The most influential aspects of your profile that contributed to this prediction were your performance rankings in your third year of studies, your LSAT score, and your first-year performance ranking. Your ranking in the third year was notably low compared to the average of accepted students, which raises concerns about your preparedness for the rigors of the bar exam. This ranking pushed the prediction toward a higher likelihood of failure.

While your LSAT score was above average, it did not sufficiently counterbalance the concerns raised by your academic rankings. In fact, your first-year ranking also fell short of the average for accepted students, further contributing to the prediction of failure. Together, these factors suggest that your academic performance may not align with the expectations for success in the bar exam.

Moving forward, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your academic performance, particularly in your remaining studies, and consider retaking the LSAT to achieve a higher score. Strengthening these areas could enhance your future applications and better position you for success in law school and beyond.
